name: Interval
description: GLMZ's most discussed and least-completed neural-feed film: a 38-minute experience in which the viewer inhabits the sensory perspective of a woman in the final moments before a stroke, with time dilated so that each second occupies roughly four minutes of subjective experience. Director Saoirse Nnadi-Castillo collaborated with neurologists to map authentic perceptual distortion — colors bleed into sound, spatial geometry becomes elastic, and memory intrudes uninvited into present sensation. Approximately 40% of viewers disengage before the end due to disorientation.
cultural_impact: Fundamentally changed the conversation about what neural-feed cinema is permitted to do to a viewer's sense of time and self, and remains the benchmark reference for every subsequent art-house neural experience.
story_hooks: The woman whose sensory experience forms the film's foundation is still alive — and she never consented to the mapping; she only recently discovered the film exists.
A corporate R&D division has been studying the film's time-dilation techniques for interrogation applications.
Someone has extended the film to 14 hours using AI-generated continuation — and the extended version contains information about the director that shouldn't be possible to know.
